item.research_question: What is the weldability (specifically remelting behavior and susceptibility to hot/cold cracks) and wear resistance of a vanadium carbide-precipitating CrCoFeMoNiV high entropy alloy?
item.material_system: Cr27.5Co14Fe22Mo22Ni11.65V2.85 (atomic percent) high entropy alloy with intended vanadium carbide precipitation
item.processing_route: Arc casting in a graphite crucible at approx. 1600 °C under argon atmosphere for 10 min with stirring; samples remelted on one side using TIG welding with 100 A current and 10 mm tip-to-workpiece distance
item.test_conditions: ASTM G75 Miller test for three-body abrasive wear (22.24 N load, 20 m/min speed, 6 hours duration, corundum F220 suspension); microstructural analysis via optical/SEM microscopy with Murakami etchant; Vickers hardness HV0.2
key_findings: The as-cast alloy hardness is 324HV0.2, rising to 339HV0.2 after TIG remelting due to accelerated cooling.
No hot cracks, cold cracks, or pore formation were observed in the TIG remelted area.
The alloy exhibits a two-phase matrix (molybdenum-rich and molybdenum-poor/nickel-rich) with vanadium-chromium carbide and intermetallic precipitates.
Wear resistance (ablation 126 mm³) is comparable to Stellite 6 (122 mm³) and Stellite 12 (91 mm³) in the ASTM G75 test.
No distinct heat-affected zone (HAZ) was observed in the remelted microstructure.
EDX analysis showed a reduction of dissolved nickel by about 6 at.% and an increase in Cr and Mo content due to slag formation during casting.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the wear resistance to the precipitation of vanadium carbides and the high hardness of the matrix. The absence of a distinct HAZ and cracks is attributed to the alloy's basic remeltability, though the presence of a low-melting second phase in the interdendritic region theoretically increases the risk of hot cracking, which was not observed under the specific test conditions without external restraints.
item.limitations: The study notes that EDX measurements have restrictions in accuracy regarding chemical composition determination. Additionally, the two-phase system with a low-melting phase creates a theoretical risk for hot cracking that was not fully validated under external stress conditions.
item.future_work: The authors propose adjusting the molybdenum content to achieve a single-phase system, increasing the carbon content to enhance carbide precipitation and wear resistance, and applying specific welding tests to determine cold cracking susceptibility.
quotes: The hardness of the as cast alloy is 324HV0.2 and after remelting the hardness rises to 339HV0.2.
Neither hot cracks nor pore formation were observed. At most, the remelted area is slightly finer in terms of its phase distribution and size.

The wear resistance of the CrCoFeMoNi + VC alloy is within the range of conventionally used wear protection alloys and clearly shows potential for a further increase in wear resistance by, for example, increasing the proportion of carbides by increasing the carbon content of the starting alloy.
